Robot Doctor Code & OpModes

Controls feel laggy or the loop is slow

Delay between the stick and the robot. Below are the 5 most common causes on FTC robots, ordered from most to least likely, with how to check and fix each one.

Skip the guesswork — run the interactive diagnosisAbout 5 quick questions narrow this list down to your robot's actual problem.

Quick checks first

  • Is your loop time above ~30 ms? Add a loop timer to telemetry (the fix below shows how). Snappy robots run around 5–20 ms.
  • Do you turn on bulk reads (LynxModule BulkCachingMode)? Search the code for setBulkCachingMode.
  • Do you read color, distance, or other I2C sensors every loop? REV color/distance sensors, external IMUs, and similar.
  • Is a camera or vision pipeline running during teleop? A VisionPortal, AprilTag processor, or Limelight streaming.
  • Is the ping on the Driver Station high (over ~50 ms) or jumping around? Ping is shown at the top of the Driver Station app while connected. About 5 ms is great.

Common causes and how to fix them

1 Every sensor read is a separate trip to the hub

Without bulk reads, each encoder or sensor read costs its own round trip, so loops crawl.

How to fix it 5 min

  1. Turn on bulk caching in AUTO mode. One line, big speedup.
  2. Measure your loop time in telemetry so you can see the difference.
Bulk reads + loop timer
for (LynxModule hub : hardwareMap.getAll(LynxModule.class)) {
    hub.setBulkCachingMode(LynxModule.BulkCachingMode.AUTO);
}

ElapsedTime loopTimer = new ElapsedTime();
// in the loop:
telemetry.addData("Loop (ms)", loopTimer.milliseconds());
loopTimer.reset();

Sources: GM0 · Bulk reads

2 Slow I2C sensors in the loop

I2C sensors (color, distance, external IMU) are not part of bulk reads, and each read takes a few milliseconds.

How to fix it 15 min

  1. Only read I2C sensors when you need them, not every loop.
  2. Cache the reading once per loop instead of calling it several times.

Sources: GM0 · Bulk reads

3 Vision is eating the processor

A camera at high resolution with live preview and several processors can slow the whole robot down.

How to fix it 10 min

  1. Turn off the live view for matches, and lower the camera resolution.
  2. Disable processors you are not using with setProcessorEnabled(..., false), or stop streaming when vision is not needed.

Sources: FTC Docs · VisionPortal CPU and bandwidth

4 Your code is blocking the robot controller

A long loop or sleep can make the robot look disconnected: ping climbs and the controls stop responding even though Wi-Fi is fine.

How to fix it 15 min

  1. Check whether the problem only happens in one OpMode. An empty OpMode with good ping means the link is fine and the code is the issue.
  2. Never sleep or loop for a long time inside an iterative OpMode's loop(). Use a timer and check it each loop instead.
  3. In LinearOpMode, every while loop must check opModeIsActive().

Sources: FTC Docs · Wireless issues at events · GM0 · Common software issues

5 Busy or blocked Wi-Fi channel

Crowded channels, school Wi-Fi suppressors, or interference make the link slow and flaky.

How to fix it 10 min

  1. Look at the ping on the Driver Station. Around 5 ms is great, under 50 ms is fine, 250 ms+ means a bad link.
  2. If your Driver Station supports it, switch the Control Hub to 5 GHz (REV recommends it), or change to a quieter channel.
  3. At school, ask IT whether a Wi-Fi suppressor is running. It will knock out any robot network.
  4. At an event, tell the FTA or CSA. They can check the channel and move you.

Sources: FTC Docs · Wireless issues at events · REV · Control Hub troubleshooting
